title: Advanced Relative Speed — Circular Tracks
tagline: Year 3 — Meeting times and meeting points of runners on a circular track

introduction.overview: On a straight road two objects meet at most once, but on a circular track runners keep meeting again and again. Two runners moving in the same direction meet when the faster has gained one full lap on the slower; in opposite directions they meet when together they have covered one full lap. The number of different meeting points on the track depends on the speed ratio. This chapter develops meeting time, meeting at the starting point and the number of meeting points.
introduction.placementRelevance: Circular-track questions are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds as a harder application of relative speed, often with the phrase "meet for the first time at the starting point".
introduction.realWorldContext: Laps on a running track, planets revolving around a star and two hands of a clock are circular-motion problems.

learningObjectives: Find the first meeting time for runners in the same and opposite directions
Find the time to meet at the starting point using lap times
Count the number of distinct meeting points
Find the distance each runner covers at the first meeting

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Relative speed = sum (opposite) or difference (same direction). Lap time = L ÷ speed. LCM gives repeated coincidence.

coreDefinitions: Lap: one complete round of the track of length L.
First meeting (same direction): L ÷ (v₁ − v₂). First meeting (opposite): L ÷ (v₁ + v₂).
Meeting at the start: the first time both are at the starting point together (LCM of lap times).
Meeting points: the number of different points on the track where meetings happen.
Speed ratio a : b in lowest terms determines the number of meeting points.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Each meeting is one lap of relative distance. Meetings happen at equal time gaps; the points where they happen shift along the track, and after a fixed number of meetings they begin to repeat. That fixed number is the count of meeting points.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: First meeting time = L ÷ relative speed. For the start point, find the smallest t with both speeds × t a multiple of L. For meeting points, reduce the speed ratio to lowest terms a : b; the count is a + b (opposite) or |a − b| (same direction).

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: First meeting
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Same: L/(v₁ − v₂);  Opposite: L/(v₁ + v₂)

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Meeting at the start
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: t = smallest value with v₁t and v₂t multiples of L
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: Lap times 50 s and 66.67 s → 200 s

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Meeting points (opposite)
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: a + b for speed ratio a : b in lowest terms

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Meeting points (same direction)
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: |a − b| for a : b in lowest terms

mainNarrative: First meeting: on a 400 m track, runners at 5 m/s and 3 m/s starting together in the same direction meet after 400 ÷ (5 − 3) = 200 s. If they run in opposite directions they meet after 400 ÷ (5 + 3) = 50 s.

To meet at the starting point, both must complete whole laps at the same time. For speeds 6 and 8 m/s on a 400 m track, 6t and 8t must both be multiples of 400: t = 200 s works (1200 m and 1600 m, that is 3 and 4 laps), and no smaller t does.

Meeting points: for speeds in the lowest-terms ratio a : b, runners moving in opposite directions meet at a + b distinct points, and runners moving in the same direction meet at |a − b| distinct points. Speeds 3 : 2 give 5 points in opposite directions; speeds 5 : 3 give 2 points in the same direction.

Distances at the first meeting: in opposite directions they cover the lap together in the ratio of their speeds. With speeds 7 and 9 on 400 m, they meet after 25 s; the faster has covered 225 m and the slower 175 m.

For three runners, find when each pair meets and take the LCM. Speeds 4, 6 and 10 m/s on 600 m (same direction) give gaps 2 and 4: meeting times 300 s and 150 s, so all three are together after LCM(300, 150) = 300 s.

deepDiveAspects.title: Why the number of meeting points is a + b
deepDiveAspects.content: In the time of one lap of relative distance the runners cover (a + b) parts of the track together; after a + b meetings the pattern returns to the start point.

deepDiveAspects.title: Lowest terms matter
deepDiveAspects.content: Always reduce the speed ratio first. Speeds 6 and 4 reduce to 3 : 2, giving 5 points, not 10.

solvedExamples.title: First meeting
solvedExamples.question: Two runners start together on a 400 m circular track at 5 m/s and 3 m/s in the same direction. After how many seconds do they first meet?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The faster gains one full lap.

solvedExamples.title: Meeting at the start
solvedExamples.question: Two runners at 6 m/s and 8 m/s run on a 400 m track from the same start. After how many seconds do they next meet at the starting point?

steps.title: Whole laps together
steps.explanation: Need 6t and 8t multiples of 400: t = 200 s.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: It is the LCM of the two lap times.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Using their first meeting time of 200 s coincidentally; the two ideas differ.

solvedExamples.title: Number of meeting points
solvedExamples.question: Two runners run in opposite directions with speeds in the ratio 3 : 2. At how many different points on the track do they meet?

shortcutMethods.title: L over relative speed

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Track both runners lap by lap.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Meeting time = L ÷ relative speed; start-point time = LCM of lap times; points = a + b or |a − b| in lowest terms.

rulesForApplication: Start-point time ≠ first meeting time in general.

commonMistakes.mistake: Confusing the first meeting with the start-point meeting

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: The time to meet at the start is a multiple of the first-meeting time.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Convert lap times to whole numbers before taking the LCM.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: The same idea gives clock-hand coincidences.

summaryBullets: Three runners: LCM of pair times.
